result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both pages show step 2 of 4 clearly, label every field and make Continue the filled primary button. A keeps the native radio buttons visible with a short description under each option, and its layout stays single column, so it meets the rubric more fully. B hides the radio circles behind styled cards and puts the three options side by side on desktop, which weakens 'visible radio options' and the single-column layout; A also adds inline validation where B relies on the browser's built-in required check. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers show progress well, show only the Incident step, and make Continue the primary action. A hides the native radio inputs behind styled cards (opacity 0) and puts the options in a three-column row, so it scores lower on visible radios and single-column layout. B keeps native radios with one-line descriptions in a full-width stacked list, uses the full step names, and adds accessible inline validation, making it the stronger design.
